sources.label: spec advance-meta rq-statusProbeCache01
sources.summary: Spec already mandates _freshness with cached_at/stale/optional error and stale-diagnostic-only safety. age_ms/ttl_ms + forceRefresh are additive extensions requiring a spec body update, not a new requirement.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: The draft design substantially overstates net-new work. forceRefresh already exists end-to-end in createProbeCache.fetch (probe-cache.ts:30,100) — no new cache plumbing is required; the only gap is (a) adding age_ms/ttl_ms to ProbeCacheFreshness computed centrally (ttlMs + cachedAtMs are already in scope at line 62/120), (b) adding an optional forceRefresh arg to adv_status and threading it into the ~5 fetchStatus* wrappers, and (c) a spec body update. The age_ms/ttl_ms naming and forceRefresh+refresh_reason shape already have a shipped precedent in backlog.ts/roadmap.ts — reuse it verbatim for cross-surface consistency. The safety boundary the draft calls out is already structurally enforced by isRestartServiceabilityVerified (serviceable && !stale) in temporal-ops.ts, which is a separate uncached verification path and must NOT consume the advisory status _freshness — the design should assert this boundary is unchanged rather than re-implement it. Summary lightness is already guaranteed by buildStatusViewPlan; no extra guard needed beyond a regression test.

validation.notes: Design is sound and low-risk because it rides existing, tested infrastructure. Recommend narrowing the design narrative to reflect that forceRefresh cache plumbing already exists, reuse backlog/roadmap freshness naming, and add an explicit test asserting temporal-ops non-stale verification does not regress to consuming status _freshness.

tradeoffs: Central age_ms/ttl_ms in ProbeCacheFreshness benefits every probe consumer uniformly but slightly widens a shared type — existing consumers (temporal-ops, status) tolerate additive optional-ish fields.

Reusing backlog/roadmap freshness naming (age_ms/ttl_ms/refresh_reason) gains cross-surface consistency at the cost of coupling two independently-evolving freshness vocabularies by convention only (no shared type).
forceRefresh on adv_status adds a diagnostic escape hatch but must be explicitly barred from authorizing safety-critical mutations, keeping the stale-diagnostic-only invariant.

alternatives_considered.option: Add age_ms/ttl_ms per-callsite in status.ts instead of centrally in createProbeCache
alternatives_considered.rationale: Duplicates Date.now()-cachedAtMs math already done in probe-cache.ts:120; central computation is DRY and covers temporal-ops reuse for free.

alternatives_considered.option: Introduce a new forceRefresh plumbing layer
alternatives_considered.rationale: createProbeCache.fetch already accepts { forceRefresh } (probe-cache.ts:30,100) and LRU forceRefresh works (proven by temporal-ops restart wait loop). No new layer needed.

alternatives_considered.option: Invent new freshness field names for status
alternatives_considered.rationale: backlog.ts/roadmap.ts already ship age_ms/ttl_ms/refresh_reason; reuse for agent-facing consistency.

alternatives_considered.option: Re-derive stale-safety guard inside status probe path
alternatives_considered.rationale: isRestartServiceabilityVerified in temporal-ops.ts is the single non-stale authority; status _freshness stays advisory. Preserve, don't duplicate.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed. Rescope design doc to: (1) extend ProbeCacheFreshness with age_ms/ttl_ms computed centrally in createProbeCache; (2) add optional forceRefresh to adv_status args and thread into existing fetchStatus* wrappers via the already-present cache option; (3) reuse backlog/roadmap freshness naming; (4) add a regression test asserting temporal-ops non-stale verification is unaffected and summary view stays light. Drop any task implying new forceRefresh cache infrastructure.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Auto-adopt central age_ms/ttl_ms and reuse of existing forceRefresh plumbing + backlog naming; surface to orchestrator the design-narrative correction that forceRefresh cache work is already done.

sources.label: lru-cache FetchOptions docs (Context7 /isaacs/node-lru-cache)
sources.summary: forceRefresh:boolean forces re-fetch even if cached and not stale. allowStaleOnFetchAbort/allowStaleOnFetchRejection return stale on bounded abort/rejection. Confirms D2 claim: forceRefresh:true refreshes (AC2) while preserving stale-on-timeout fallback (AC4).

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Design is additive over an already-correct probe-cache architecture. All four key anchors verified in source: (1) createProbeCache centrally derives freshness at the cache boundary and already threads forceRefresh; (2) buildStatusViewPlan selects advisory probes per view; (3) applyStatusView projects _freshness only in health view, guaranteeing summary lightness structurally; (4) isRestartServiceabilityVerified enforces serviceable && !stale for safety-critical restart. Adding age_ms/ttl_ms to ProbeCacheFreshness and a public adv_status.forceRefresh confined to view-plan-selected advisory caches does not touch status load, change/task/gate reads, contract state, archive decisions, mutation readiness, Temporal replay surface, or spec/tool boundaries. lru-cache forceRefresh + stale-on-abort/rejection semantics are documented and already configured (allowStale/allowStaleOnFetchAbort/allowStaleOnFetchRejection/ignoreFetchAbort). Naming reuse (age_ms/ttl_ms) matches backlog/roadmap freshness precedent. Updating rq-statusProbeCache01 in place (D5) rather than minting a new requirement is correct: the new fields are a superset of the same requirement's freshness contract.

validation.notes: One non-blocking clarity note: summary view plan has temporalHealth:true, so adv_status forceRefresh on the default summary view WILL force-refresh the temporal_health probe. This is consistent with AC2 (forceRefresh refreshes selected advisory probes) and does not violate AC3 (summary projection still emits only temporal_health_ok, no _freshness). Recommend implementation tests explicitly cover forceRefresh on summary to lock the lightweight-projection invariant. No correctness-state or safety-critical caching is introduced; DONT/C constraints respected.

tradeoffs: Exposing a public forceRefresh on adv_status adds an operator-facing knob and a small test-surface obligation to keep it advisory-only and view-plan-scoped.
Enriching ProbeCacheFreshness centrally couples every probe consumer to the new age_ms/ttl_ms fields, but this is desirable superset behavior and matches existing backlog/roadmap freshness naming.
Amending rq-statusProbeCache01 in place keeps one requirement authoritative but requires regenerating/validating scenarios so age_ms/ttl_ms and status-facing forceRefresh are covered.

alternatives_considered.option: Separate dedicated freshness cache layer for status
alternatives_considered.rationale: Duplicates the existing createProbeCache boundary; violates simplicity/LBP and the C1 no-unrelated-refactor constraint. Central enrichment reuses proven code.
Fails AC2 which requires operators to force a refresh via forceRefresh:true. lru-cache already supports the option, so exposing it is the minimal path.

alternatives_considered.option: Emit full detailed _freshness in the summary view
alternatives_considered.rationale: Violates AC3/D3 lightweight-summary requirement; applyStatusView already correctly restricts _freshness to the health view.

alternatives_considered.option: Mint a new requirement instead of amending rq-statusProbeCache01
alternatives_considered.rationale: The new age_ms/ttl_ms/forceRefresh behavior is a superset of the same freshness contract; a second requirement would fragment the law (AC6 explicitly asks to update rq-statusProbeCache01).

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed with the design as written. During implementation, add explicit tests that (a) forceRefresh:true on the summary view force-refreshes temporal_health while the summary projection still omits _freshness, and (b) age_ms/ttl_ms appear only in health-view _freshness, to lock the diagnostic-only + lightweight-summary invariants.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Design PASSES validation. It is an additive, boring extension over the existing probe-cache architecture with no spec-law contradiction: rq-statusProbeCache01 is amended (not duplicated), the stale-safety guard isRestartServiceabilityVerified is preserved, summary lightness is structurally enforced by applyStatusView, and lru-cache forceRefresh/stale-on-abort semantics are documented and already configured. No simpler viable alternative exists that still satisfies AC2's operator-facing forceRefresh. Proceed to planning; only add targeted tests for forceRefresh-on-summary and age_ms/ttl_ms placement.

documents.proposal:
# Add status health probe TTL

## Why

Frequent `adv_status` health views can pay repeated Temporal, task-queue, worker-diagnostic, search-attribute, snapshot-health, and worktree-census probe costs. ADV needs bounded TTL reuse for advisory health probes so status remains fast and less noisy, while correctness-critical ADV truth (changes, gates, tasks, archive/recovery authority) stays live and uncached by this optimization.

This work is linked to GitHub issue #107 and Epic `optimizeAdvPerformanceStructure` entry `Add status health probe TTL`.

## What Changes

Validate and complete bounded TTL caching for ADV status health probes. Existing source already shows a `createProbeCache` abstraction and status health probe caches in `plugin/src/tools/status-health.ts`; discovery should determine whether those implementations fully satisfy issue #107 and `rq-statusProbeCache01`, or whether gaps remain around coverage, force-refresh behavior, cache-age presentation, stale fallback semantics, tests, or non-cancellable underlying probes.

## User Outcomes

- Status/health output remains responsive during repeated agent/operator checks.
- Operators can tell whether health details are fresh or cached/stale before acting on them.
- ADV avoids redundant Temporal/worker probe noise on common status paths.
- Safety-critical workflow state remains trustworthy and is not hidden behind advisory caches.

## Scope

### In Scope

- Advisory health probes used by `adv_status`, especially Temporal health, task-queue serviceability, worker diagnostics, search-attribute health, snapshot health, and worktree census.
- Freshness metadata surfaced with cached timestamp and stale/error signal where health probe cache data appears.
- Tests proving cache hit/miss behavior, stale fallback behavior, and safety boundary behavior for cached probe output.
- Spec-law alignment with `advance-meta` `rq-statusProbeCache01`; add or adjust spec law only if discovery finds the issue requires behavior not already covered.

### Out of Scope

- Caching change, gate, task, contract, archive, or release truth.
- Making stale cached health data sufficient proof for worker-lock reclaim, restart success, overrides, unlocks, archive decisions, or gate completion.
- Broad status/dashboard refactors not needed to satisfy this health-probe TTL outcome.
- OCA-specific work and unrelated cleanup not tied to health-probe performance or correctness.

### Must Not

- Must not cache correctness-critical ADV state such as tasks, gates, change lifecycle, acceptance/release evidence, or archive eligibility.
- Must not weaken Temporal replay safety, typed tool boundaries, or spec-law checks.
- Must not hide unhealthy states beyond the bounded TTL window without explicit stale/freshness metadata.
- Must not authorize safety-critical mutations from stale cached diagnostics.

## Affected Code

- `plugin/src/tools/status.ts` — status view orchestration and `_freshness` output.
- `plugin/src/tools/status-health.ts` — health probe cache wiring and queue-serviceability computation.
- `plugin/src/tools/probe-cache.ts` — reusable TTL/stale fallback abstraction.
- `plugin/src/tools/status.test.ts`, `plugin/src/tools/probe-cache.test.ts`, and related Temporal diagnostics tests — cache and freshness coverage.
- `.adv/specs/advance-meta` — existing spec law includes `rq-statusProbeCache01`; update only if discovery confirms a spec gap.

## Related Repositories

- Current repo only: `/home/jon/dev/advance`.

## Constraints

- ADV/Temporal state remains source of truth.
- Implementation must use the `change/addStatusHealthProbeTtl` worktree for mutations.
- Source edits to plugin tool behavior require source tests now; live tool behavior requires rebuild/deploy/restart before end-to-end validation in a fresh session.
- Existing project wisdom notes that source tests can pass before live deployed plugin behavior changes.

## Impact

Expected impact is localized performance and reliability improvement for status/health diagnostics. The risky boundary is false confidence from cached/stale health data; that boundary must stay explicit and tested.

## Context

Epic reconnaissance identified performance-sensitive status/dashboard/Temporal visibility paths. Issue #107 specifically calls out repeated health probes in `adv_status` and asks for bounded TTL caching while preserving raw health detail in `view: health`.

Quick checks found:

- `status-health.ts` already defines `STATUS_PROBE_TTL_MS`, `statusTemporalHealthProbeCache`, `statusQueueServiceabilityProbeCache`, `statusSearchAttributesProbeCache`, `snapshotHealthProbeCache`, and `statusWorktreeCensusProbeCache`.
- `probe-cache.ts` already supports `forceRefresh`, stale fallback, timeout signals, and freshness fields.
- `adv_status view: "health"` currently returns `_freshness` entries for temporal health, queue serviceability, search attributes, worktree census, and snapshot health.
- `advance-meta` already contains `rq-statusProbeCache01` for bounded cached health probes and diagnostic-only stale data.

## Discovery Agenda

- Determine whether issue #107 is already fully implemented by current source, partially implemented, or only present in undeployed/runtime-divergent code.
- Verify whether a user/tool-level force-refresh control is required for `adv_status`, or whether internal probe-cache `forceRefresh` support is sufficient.
- Verify whether “cached age” should remain derivable from `cached_at` or be surfaced as explicit `age_ms` / TTL metadata.
- Confirm all underlying probes either forward `AbortSignal` to cancellable work or are explicitly bounded/classified per `rq-statusProbeCache01`.
- Confirm tests cover cache hit/miss, stale fallback, freshness output, and safety boundaries that prevent cached data from authorizing critical mutations.
- Decide whether `rq-statusProbeCache01` needs a spec amendment for force-refresh or explicit cache-age metadata.

## Discovery Findings

### Discovery Checklist

| Step | Status | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Skill Discovery | PASS | Checked trusted skills; loaded `adv-improve` because prior repo performance pack is directly relevant. Pending-review scan found no pending skill frontmatter; one literal example line in `adv-skill-author` was not a real pending skill. |

| Conflict & Related-Work Scan | PASS | `adv_change_list includeArchived` showed this change plus related archived `diagnoseArchivedListingTimeout2`; validation passed with expected pre-prep warnings `NO_TASKS` and `NO_DELTAS`; agenda has many unrelated subagent follow-ups but no direct status-probe TTL owner. |

| LBP Check | PASS | Internal/status-local change; external alternative adoption skipped. Existing `lru-cache` usage remains LBP per prior Context7-cited research pack. |
| Completeness Verification | PASS | Problem covers advisory status health probes, not all ADV state. No sole-entry claim required; secondary surfaces classified below. |

### Skills Considered

- `adv-improve`: matched performance/status optimization and prior research-pack extension; loaded and applied for evidence-backed improvement framing.
- `adv-opportunity-scout`: considered but not run; this is a narrow health-probe TTL completion, not broad strategy/product/external-option scope.
- No new skill created; existing skills cover the relevant internal performance/discovery method.

### Extends

- `docs/repo-improve-prep.md`:
  - Relevant prior finding: probe caching foundation was already classified SOUND, citing `lru-cache` `cache.fetch()` coalescing and stale-on-abort/rejection behavior.
  - Relevant prior applicability: status/default path performance and health/probe substep attribution were high-value optimization areas.
  - New finding: the pack's line 107 anti-pattern about full status output being built before projection is stale for current source. `plugin/src/tools/status-view.ts:40-79` now computes a per-view execution plan, and `plugin/src/tools/status.test.ts:793-810` asserts summary skips detailed providers.
- Archived change `diagnoseArchivedListingTimeout2`:
  - Relevant lesson: terminal aggregate/list performance work preserved active fast paths and emitted structured degraded metadata rather than raising timeouts.
  - New finding: this change should follow the same pattern: keep status summary light and expose degradation/freshness explicitly instead of hiding probe failures.

### Conflict Scan

- Active/related changes:
  - `addStatusHealthProbeTtl` is current target.
  - `diagnoseArchivedListingTimeout2` archived and related by Epic/performance structure; informs performance/safety style but does not own status health TTL.
  - `diagnoseArchivedListingTimeout` stale draft appears to be superseded by archived `diagnoseArchivedListingTimeout2`; no direct conflict with this scope.
- `adv_change_validate`: pass. Warnings `NO_TASKS` and `NO_DELTAS` are expected before planning/spec-delta work.
- `adv_agenda_list`: many pending subagent follow-ups; none directly target `adv_status` health probe TTL/force-refresh/age metadata.

### Current State

- `plugin/src/tools/probe-cache.ts` defines `ProbeCacheFreshness` with `cached_at`, `stale`, optional `error`, and `ProbeCache.fetch(key, { forceRefresh })`.
- `plugin/src/tools/status-health.ts` defines status caches:
  - `STATUS_PROBE_TTL_MS = 2_000` for temporal health, worktree census, search attributes, and queue serviceability.
  - `SNAPSHOT_HEALTH_TTL_MS = 60_000` for snapshot health.
  - Temporal health and worktree census forward `AbortSignal` to cancellable providers.
  - Queue serviceability wraps `getTemporalWorkerDiagnostics()` and `probeTaskQueuePollers()`; this path is bounded by the outer probe-cache timeout but `probeTaskQueuePollers()` itself does not accept an AbortSignal.
- `plugin/src/tools/status.ts` collects `_freshness` for health probes and exposes it in `view: "health"`. Current `adv_status` args do not expose `forceRefresh`.
- `plugin/src/tools/status-view.ts` has lazy view planning. Summary runs temporal health only and skips queue serviceability, search attributes, worktree census, snapshot health, and session debt.
- Tests cover generic probe cache coalescing, TTL refresh, stale-on-abort, stale-on-reject, cold failure, and cold timeout (`probe-cache.test.ts`). Status tests cover health-view freshness reuse and AbortSignal forwarding for temporal health/worktree census. They do not yet cover status-level force-refresh, explicit `age_ms`/`ttl_ms`, queue-serviceability force refresh, or snapshot/search freshness age.

### Edge Cases

1. Force-refresh gap:
   - Fresh cached value exists but operator just restarted worker or registered search attributes; status must allow bypassing cache for advisory probes.
   - Force refresh fails while stale value exists; output may return stale value, but must mark `stale: true` with error and must not treat it as serviceability proof.
2. Freshness-age gap:
   - Consumers should not need to parse `cached_at` and know each probe TTL to tell how old a result is.
   - Different probes have different TTLs (2s status probes, 60s snapshot health, 30s nested poller cache), so freshness should identify the TTL/budget actually governing each probe.
3. Non-cancellable probe behavior:
   - `probeTaskQueuePollers()` lacks an AbortSignal parameter; outer cache timeout bounds caller wait but underlying provider may still continue.
   - `scanSnapshotHealth()` is longer-budget work; status cache timeout bounds cold wait to 10s and caches results, but tests should preserve that classification.
4. Safety boundary:
   - A stale queue-serviceability result must not authorize worker-lock reclaim or worker-restart success.
   - Summary view should not grow detailed `_freshness` output if that defeats the lightweight orientation path.

### Open Design Questions

1. Public force-refresh shape
   - Trust model: agent-owned technical choice, user-visible behavior.
   - Blast radius: schema/API compatibility and caller expectations.
   - Alternatives: add `forceRefresh?: boolean` to `adv_status`; add only to `view:"health"`; create separate health-refresh tool. Recommendation: add optional `forceRefresh` to `adv_status`, applying only to advisory probe caches.
2. Freshness metadata shape
   - Trust model: joint; affects operator readability.
   - Blast radius: additive output schema and tests.
   - Alternatives: keep `cached_at` only; add `age_ms`; add `age_ms` + `ttl_ms` + `refresh_requested` where relevant. Recommendation: additive `age_ms` and `ttl_ms`, with refresh marker when requested.
3. Summary view visibility
   - Trust model: joint; affects common agent output noise/performance.
   - Blast radius: default status response size and hot-path latency.
   - Alternatives: expose `_freshness` in summary; keep only `temporal_health_ok`; require `view:"health"` for cache detail. Recommendation: keep summary lightweight and expose detailed freshness in health/hygiene diagnostic views only.
4. Spec law update
   - Trust model: agent-owned spec-law decision after user confirms outcome.
   - Blast radius: future tests and tool behavior.
   - Alternatives: rely on current `rq-statusProbeCache01`; modify it to require age/TTL and force-refresh for status health; add a new requirement. Recommendation: modify `rq-statusProbeCache01` because this is an evolution of the existing bounded cached health probes law.

### Draft Spec Deltas

Modify `advance-meta` `rq-statusProbeCache01`:

- Add that status-facing cached health probe freshness must include `cached_at`, `stale`, optional `error`, `age_ms`, and `ttl_ms`.
- Add that `adv_status` must expose a force-refresh request path for advisory probe caches, and force-refresh must not bypass correctness/safety checks.

Scenario draft:

- Given two `adv_status view:"health"` calls within the probe TTL, when the second call omits force refresh, then it reuses cached advisory probe values and returns freshness metadata including `cached_at`, `age_ms`, `ttl_ms`, and `stale:false`.
- Given an `adv_status view:"health"` call with force refresh requested, when advisory probe caches contain fresh values, then the status read attempts fresh probes for each requested advisory probe and marks the response as refresh-requested without caching or bypassing gate/task/change truth.
- Given force refresh times out or fails after a last-known-good value exists, when the status read returns stale advisory data, then `_freshness.*.stale` is true with an error summary and the stale data is diagnostic-only.

### Related Pattern Scan

- `plugin/src/tools/temporal-ops.ts`: restart verification uses `forceRefresh: true` and `isRestartServiceabilityVerified()` requires `!freshness.stale`; adopt safety pattern for tests and reasoning, but do not reuse stale status probes for mutations.
- `plugin/src/tools/backlog.ts`: public `forceRefresh` argument and freshness refresh marker pattern exists for backlog; useful output-shape precedent.
- `plugin/src/temporal/health-probe.ts`: nested 30s poller cache exists; discovery should avoid double-counting it as `adv_status` TTL and should expose only the status probe TTL unless design chooses nested metadata.
- `plugin/src/tools/target-project.ts`: direct worker diagnostics support target mutation readiness. Out of scope because mutation readiness is safety-critical and should not depend on stale advisory status cache.
- No similar status-health probe TTL gaps found outside status/temporal diagnostics surfaces.

### Completeness Verification

- Problem-completeness: High confidence. The full problem is not merely repeated `getTemporalHealth()`; it covers advisory status health probe freshness/force-refresh semantics across temporal health, queue serviceability, search attributes, snapshot health, and worktree census.
- Solution-scope: High confidence. Scope is not a broad status rewrite; current lazy view planning and cache abstractions already exist. Intended solution is additive: expose force refresh/age metadata, close tests/spec gaps, preserve diagnostic-only stale semantics.
- Sole-entry claim: Not asserted. Discovery does not rely on one global cache chokepoint for all ADV diagnostics.
- Secondary surfaces:
  - `temporal-ops.ts` recovery diagnostics: related, in scope only for safety-pattern verification; no behavioral change unless design finds a shared helper is necessary.
  - `target-project.ts` mutation readiness: out of scope with rationale; safety-critical readiness must remain fresh/proven.
  - `health-probe.ts` nested poller cache: out of scope except documentation/test awareness; it is lower-level Temporal health behavior.

### LBP Check

- Long-term best practice is to keep deterministic view plans and bounded cached diagnostic probes, while keeping correctness state live and structurally guarded. Current source aligns with that direction.
- External-solution check skipped: this is an internal ADV status/tooling change with no realistic external library/service alternative. Prior `repo-improve-prep.md` already cites `lru-cache` docs and classifies current cache foundation as SOUND.
- Opportunity scout skipped: narrow low-opportunity completion of an existing internal probe-cache contract; broader performance opportunities already captured by the Epic and `repo-improve-prep.md`.

### Recommended Objectives

1. Add or verify public force-refresh behavior for `adv_status` advisory health probes.
2. Add explicit cache age/TTL freshness metadata for status health probe outputs.
3. Keep stale cached health data diagnostic-only and never authoritative for safety-critical mutations/recovery/release decisions.
4. Preserve lazy status view behavior; summary remains lightweight and detailed probe metadata stays in diagnostic views unless user chooses otherwise.
5. Add focused tests covering status-level cache hit/miss, force-refresh, stale fallback, age/TTL metadata, and safety boundaries.
6. Update `rq-statusProbeCache01` if agreement confirms force-refresh/age metadata as durable behavior.

### AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS

M1 MEDIUM Missing Information Public force-refresh and cache-age output shape need user confirmation before criteria are finalized.
  Evidence: "Verify whether a user/tool-level force-refresh control is required for `adv_status`, or whether internal probe-cache `forceRefresh` support is sufficient."
  Reason: unclear because current proposal identifies both options but does not choose output/API shape.

## Problem

Frequent `adv_status` health views can pay repeated Temporal, task-queue, worker-diagnostic, search-attribute, snapshot-health, and worktree-census probe costs. ADV needs bounded TTL reuse for advisory health probes so status remains fast and less noisy, while correctness-critical ADV truth (changes, gates, tasks, archive/recovery authority) stays live and uncached by this optimization.

## Desired Outcome

Operators and agents get responsive status/health output with visible cache freshness, and stale cached health data is never treated as authority for safety-critical mutations or release decisions.

## Confirmed Scope

This change tracks GitHub issue #107 and Epic entry `optimizeAdvPerformanceStructure` / `Add status health probe TTL`. It should validate existing status probe caching, close any gaps, and preserve spec-law behavior under `advance-meta` requirement `rq-statusProbeCache01`.

# Agreement

## Objectives

1. Add or verify public force-refresh behavior for `adv_status` advisory health probes.
2. Add explicit cache age/TTL freshness metadata for status health probe outputs.
3. Keep stale cached health data diagnostic-only and never authoritative for safety-critical mutations, recovery, release, archive, gate, task, or change lifecycle decisions.
4. Preserve lazy status view behavior: default summary stays lightweight; detailed probe metadata stays in diagnostic health surfaces.
5. Add focused tests covering status-level cache hit/miss, force-refresh, stale fallback, age/TTL metadata, and safety boundaries.
6. Update or validate `advance-meta` `rq-statusProbeCache01` to cover force-refresh plus age/TTL freshness semantics.

## Success Criteria

1. Repeated `adv_status` health checks avoid redundant advisory probe work within bounded TTL windows.
2. Operators can see cache freshness without parsing timestamps: `cached_at`, `stale`, `age_ms`, `ttl_ms`, optional `error`.
3. Stale cached diagnostics remain diagnostic-only and never authorize recovery, release, archive, gate, task, or change correctness decisions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `adv_status view:"health"` returns `_freshness` for each executed status health probe with `cached_at`, `stale`, `age_ms`, `ttl_ms`, and optional `error`; `age_ms >= 0`, `ttl_ms > 0`. [warrant: tool:adv_status, spec:rq-statusProbeCache01]
2. Two `adv_status view:"health"` calls within TTL reuse advisory probe cache entries, while `forceRefresh:true` attempts fresh advisory probe fetches despite existing fresh cache. [warrant: tool:adv_status]
3. Default `adv_status view:"summary"` remains lightweight: no detailed `_freshness`, no queue-serviceability/search-attribute/snapshot-health/worktree-census diagnostic payloads. [warrant: tool:adv_status]
4. If a health probe refresh fails or times out after last-known-good data exists, returned data is marked `stale:true` with an error summary and remains advisory only. [warrant: spec:rq-statusProbeCache01]
5. Stale cached health/serviceability data cannot prove worker restart success, lock reclaim safety, override/unlock/archive readiness, gate completion, task truth, or change lifecycle truth. [warrant: spec:rq-statusProbeCache01]
6. `advance-meta` `rq-statusProbeCache01` is updated or validated to cover force-refresh plus age/TTL freshness semantics with Given/When/Then scenarios. [warrant: spec:rq-statusProbeCache01]
7. Existing raw health detail in `view:"health"` remains present for legacy consumers where the selected view plan executes that probe. [warrant: tool:adv_status]

## Constraints

1. ADV/Temporal state remains source of truth.
2. Implementation must use the `change/addStatusHealthProbeTtl` worktree for mutations.
3. Source tests may validate code in-session; live deployed ADV tool behavior requires rebuild, deploy-local sync, and OpenCode/plugin-host restart.
4. Criteria must remain design-independent: implementation may choose helper shape, metadata enrichment location, and test seams during design.
5. Stale cached diagnostics are advisory-only even when they are recent enough to return from cache.

## Avoidances

1. Do not cache correctness-critical ADV state such as tasks, gates, change lifecycle, acceptance/release evidence, or archive eligibility.
2. Do not weaken Temporal replay safety, typed tool boundaries, or spec-law checks.
3. Do not hide unhealthy states beyond the bounded TTL window without explicit stale/freshness metadata.
4. Do not authorize safety-critical mutations from stale cached diagnostics.
5. Do not broaden into unrelated status/dashboard refactors or OCA-specific work.

## Out of Scope

1. Caching change, gate, task, contract, archive, or release truth.
2. Making stale cached health data sufficient proof for worker-lock reclaim, restart success, overrides, unlocks, archive decisions, or gate completion.
3. Broad status/dashboard refactors not needed to satisfy health-probe TTL outcome.
4. OCA-specific work and unrelated cleanup not tied to health-probe performance or correctness.
5. Changing target-project mutation readiness behavior except to prove it remains independent from advisory status cache data.

## Preview Applicability

# Design

## Architecture Overview

Use the existing status probe-cache architecture; do not add a parallel cache layer.

Additive design:

1. Extend `ProbeCacheFreshness` centrally with `age_ms` and `ttl_ms`.
2. Add optional `forceRefresh?: boolean` to `adv_status`.
3. Thread `forceRefresh` only into advisory status probe cache reads selected by `buildStatusViewPlan(view)`.
4. Preserve default summary lightness: no detailed `_freshness`, queue-serviceability, search-attribute, snapshot-health, or worktree-census diagnostic payloads.
5. Preserve stale-data safety boundary: stale/advisory status freshness cannot authorize worker restart success, lock reclaim, gate/task/change truth, overrides, unlocks, archive readiness, or release decisions.
6. Update or validate `advance-meta` `rq-statusProbeCache01` for age/TTL and force-refresh semantics.

## Key Decisions

### D1 — Compute freshness fields in `createProbeCache`

`createProbeCache()` already owns `ttlMs`, `cachedAtMs`, `cached_at`, stale calculation, timeout handling, and stale fallback. Add `age_ms` and `ttl_ms` there.

- `ttl_ms = ttlMs`
- `age_ms = Math.max(0, Date.now() - entry.cachedAtMs)`
- Existing `cached_at`, `stale`, and optional `error` remain unchanged.

This keeps freshness structural and prevents each status caller from re-deriving age differently.

### D2 — `adv_status.forceRefresh` is advisory-only

Add optional `forceRefresh?: boolean` to `adv_status` args. It applies only to the advisory probe caches selected by the current view plan.

Context7 `/isaacs/node-lru-cache` documentation confirms `cache.fetch(k, { forceRefresh: true })` forces a re-fetch even when a cached value is present and fresh. It also documents stale-on-abort/rejection behavior, matching the existing `createProbeCache` stale fallback model.

`forceRefresh` must not affect:

- `loadStatusWithBootstrapRetry`
- change/task/gate/contract reads
- archive/release decisions
- worker-lock reclaim or mutation readiness
- any safety-critical proof path

### D3 — Keep default summary lightweight

Do not expose detailed `_freshness` in default `adv_status view:"summary"`.

`status-view.ts` already projects `_freshness` only for `view:"health"`; summary keeps a compact health bit. `forceRefresh:true` on summary may refresh the selected summary temporal-health probe, but summary still does not expose detailed `_freshness` or detailed diagnostic payloads.

### D4 — Stale data remains diagnostic-only

Preserve `temporal-ops.ts` non-stale proof pattern: serviceability proof requires serviceable status and non-stale freshness. Status `_freshness` is operator-visible diagnostic data, not recovery authority.

### D5 — Amend existing spec law, not new law

`advance-meta` `rq-statusProbeCache01` already owns bounded cached health probes. Amend it in place to require:

- `age_ms`
- `ttl_ms`
- status-facing advisory `forceRefresh`
- diagnostic-only stale behavior under refresh failure/timeouts

## ADR Drafts

None. Decisions refine existing helper/tool contracts and are not hard-to-reverse enough for ADR.

## Implementation Strategy

1. **Probe cache**
   - Update `plugin/src/tools/probe-cache.ts` `ProbeCacheFreshness` with `age_ms` and `ttl_ms`.
   - Compute fields in `createProbeCache().fetch()`.
   - Add tests in `plugin/src/tools/probe-cache.test.ts` for fresh, stale-on-abort, stale-on-reject, cold failure/timeout shapes.

2. **Status tool API**
   - Add `forceRefresh?: boolean` to `adv_status` args in `plugin/src/tools/status.ts`.
   - Pass `{ forceRefresh }` into each advisory probe cache read selected by `buildStatusViewPlan(view)`.
   - Update arg description: advisory health probes only; correctness state unaffected.

3. **Status health wrappers**
   - Update `fetchStatusTemporalHealth`, `fetchStatusQueueServiceability`, and `fetchStatusSnapshotHealth` to accept `{ forceRefresh?: boolean }`.
   - Keep `statusQueueServiceabilityInputs.set()` before fetch, even on force refresh.

4. **Spec law**
   - Amend `.adv/specs/advance-meta` `rq-statusProbeCache01` body and scenarios.
   - Run schema/spec drift checks as planned in prep.

5. **Tests**
   - Health view `_freshness` entries include `cached_at`, `stale`, `age_ms`, `ttl_ms`, optional `error`.
   - Repeated health calls reuse cached probes within TTL.
   - `forceRefresh:true` triggers fresh advisory probe fetch despite fresh cache.
   - Summary omits detailed `_freshness` and detailed diagnostic payloads, including when `forceRefresh:true` refreshes summary temporal health.
   - Stale fallback marks `stale:true` with `error`.
   - Stale serviceability freshness cannot satisfy `isRestartServiceabilityVerified()`.

## LBP Analysis

Preferred long-term approach: minimal structural extension of existing `createProbeCache` + status view plan.

Why:

- Reuses tested cache abstraction.
- Keeps correctness structural at cache boundary.
- Preserves lazy view planning and fast default status output.
- Keeps safety-critical recovery/mutation checks independent from advisory status diagnostics.
- Aligns with `docs/repo-improve-prep.md`, which classified existing `lru-cache` foundation as SOUND.

Rejected alternatives:

- Separate status-only cache layer — unnecessary drift and more code.
- Internal-only refresh — fails user-approved operator need.
- Full `_freshness` in summary — violates AC3 and performance/noise goal.
- Status `_freshness` as recovery proof — violates `rq-statusProbeCache01` and DONT4.

## Affected Components

- `plugin/src/tools/probe-cache.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/status.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/status-health.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/status-view.ts` tests only / guard behavior
- `plugin/src/tools/temporal-ops.ts` tests only / guard behavior
- `plugin/src/tools/probe-cache.test.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/status.test.ts`
- `plugin/src/tools/temporal-ops.test.ts`
- `.adv/specs/advance-meta`
- asset/spec docs tests that mirror stability docs and `rq-statusProbeCache01`

## Design-Derived Criteria

1. Freshness metadata is generated at the cache boundary.
2. `forceRefresh` is an advisory probe-cache option only.
3. Default summary must not expose detailed `_freshness` or detailed diagnostic payloads.
4. Status-level force refresh must preserve timeout/stale fallback behavior.
5. Safety-critical serviceability proof remains structurally non-stale.

## Risks / Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| `forceRefresh` appears to refresh correctness truth | Arg description and tests say advisory health probes only. |
| New fields break consumers | Additive fields only; existing fields unchanged. |
| Summary gets heavier | Regression test for summary with and without `forceRefresh:true`. |
| Non-cancellable lower-level probe continues after timeout | Outer probe-cache timeout/stale behavior remains; classify as bounded diagnostic work. |
| Stale health leaks into recovery authority | Preserve `temporal-ops` fresh verification path and add regression. |
| Spec-law drift | Amend/validate `rq-statusProbeCache01` and run spec/schema checks. |

## Design Leverage Scout

Scout attempted with `adv-researcher` on 2026-07-07.

- Candidates considered: 5.
- Auto-adopted: existing `forceRefresh` plumbing, central `age_ms`/`ttl_ms`, backlog/roadmap freshness naming precedent.
- Surfaced/adopted invariants: preserve temporal-ops stale-safety guard and summary lightness.
- Result: pass, high confidence, low risk.

## Validator Result

Independent `adv-researcher` validation: pass, high confidence, low risk.

Validator findings:

- `createProbeCache` already owns force-refresh pass-through and freshness boundary; design is minimal additive work.
- `status-view.ts` projects `_freshness` only in health view; summary lightness is structurally aligned.
- `temporal-ops.ts` uses `serviceable && !stale` for restart-serviceability proof; stale-safety boundary is intact.
- Context7 `lru-cache` docs support `forceRefresh` and stale-on-abort/rejection behavior.
- `rq-statusProbeCache01` is the correct spec-law anchor; proposed fields extend it without contradiction.

Validator non-blocking note:

- `buildStatusViewPlan("summary")` has `temporalHealth:true`; therefore `adv_status { view:"summary", forceRefresh:true }` may refresh temporal-health probe. This is consistent with AC2 and does not violate AC3 as long as summary still omits detailed `_freshness`.

Recommendation: proceed to planning.

## Why It Matters
